data.name: Dayasri
data.gender_notes: Dayasri is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dayasri is a Sanskrit name derived from the goddess of compassion, Shri Devi. The name is composed of two words: Daya (compassion) and Sri (goddess). It is believed that the name Dayasri bestows upon the child the divine qualities of compassion, kindness, and mercy. The name Dayasri carries the meaning “Goddess of Compassion” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dayasri usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of compassion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Infused with the divine compassion of Shri Devi
data.etymology: Dayasri belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Compassion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dayasri total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Dayasri was an important figure in the Chalukya dynasty of Karnataka, India. She was a queen consort of King Vijayaditya (1086-1118 CE). Dayasri is known for her patronage of various temples, especially the Chennakeshava temple at Belur.
historical_references.context: Chalukya Dynasty, Karnataka, India, Queen Consort, Temple Patronage

historical_references.reference: Dayasri is also mentioned in the Puranic literature as the daughter of King Mahasena of Kalinga (Orissa, India). She is described as a devotee of Lord Vishnu and is known for her penance and dedication to the god.
historical_references.context: Puranic Literature, Kalinga (Orissa), India, Devotee, Penance
